instructions: At least 4 hours ahead, or up to 24 hours: pat the steak dry. Score the top in a diamond pattern about 1 inch apart, cutting 1/8 inch deep.

In a bowl, whisk the tamari, canola oil, honey, 3 minced garlic cloves, the grated ginger, chili powder, cumin and pepper. Put the steak in a zip-top bag, pour in the marinade, press out the air and seal. Refrigerate, turning the bag over now and then.
Heat the grill to high and wipe the grates with a little oil.
Lift the steak out, shake off the extra marinade, and throw the rest of the marinade away. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, without moving it.
You're cooking it to 130°F in the middle for medium rare, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a small slit in the center: it should be rosy pink, not red and not gray.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Slice it very thin, about 1/8 inch, going across the grain.
Taste a slice. If it's flat, sprinkle on a pinch of salt.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate at least 4 hours ahead (up to 24 hours)
method_notes: Well Plated leads (4.92 from 24 ratings): a soy, oil and honey marinade with garlic, ginger, chili powder and cumin, at least 4 hours, then high-heat grilling 3 to 4 minutes a side, a 10 minute rest and thin slicing across the grain. It is the only flank steak page I could read in full, because the other well-known ones blocked me. Tamari replaces low-sodium soy sauce to keep it gluten-free, and the chili powder is kept to 1 teaspoon so the base is mild. No grill? Broil on a preheated pan 6 inches from the heat for 6 to 8 minutes without flipping.
